title: In 1582, Ten Days Vanished From the Calendar. Here's Why

scenes.text: In 1582, ten days vanished from the calendar.
People went to bed on October 4th and woke up on October 15th.
The old Roman calendar ran eleven minutes too long each year. By 1582 it was ten days off.
So the Pope cut ten days out. Catholic countries obeyed. Everyone else refused.
Britain held out until 1752. By then it was eleven days behind, and jumped from September 2nd to the 14th.
Ten days, gone. And nobody ever got them back.

description:
In 1582, ten days vanished from the calendar.
The Julian calendar ran about eleven minutes too long each year, and by 1582 the spring equinox had slipped ten days. Pope Gregory XIII fixed it by jumping straight from October 4th to October 15th. Catholic countries followed at once, but Britain waited until 1752, when it had to drop eleven days.
If you could skip ten days, which ten would you pick? Comment below.
first_comment: Bonus: for 170 years you could cross from France into England and arrive before you left, on paper. If you could delete ten days from this year, which ten would go?
